attribution: kkawamura — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Sea ice floes drifting off the Shiretoko Peninsula coast in winter
caption: Drift ice (ryūhyō) packed against the Okhotsk coast of the Shiretoko Peninsula. It arrives from the Amur River region around late January and usually leaves by early April, and the second half of February is typically its best period, which sets the timing of this whole trip.

attribution: kkawamura — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Sheets of drift ice on the Okhotsk Sea
caption: Sheets of drift ice near the Utoro and Rausu coast. In Utoro, guided drift-ice walks put you in a dry suit on the floes for about two hours; the ice moves with wind and tide, so tours are cancelled or altered when it is unsafe.

attribution: kkawamura — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The sightseeing icebreaker Aurora pushing through drift ice at Abashiri
caption: The icebreaker Aurora out of Abashiri, the most accessible way to reach the ice from a town with an airport. Sailings run roughly from late January to late March, and when no ice has arrived the ship runs a sea excursion instead.

commonsFile: File:Hokkaido-Shiretoko's White-tailed Eagles and Steller's Sea Eagles・・hiretoko National Park・・xl.jpg
attribution: koichi_hayakawa — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: White-tailed eagles and Steller's sea eagles perched on drift ice near Rausu
caption: Steller's sea eagles and white-tailed eagles on the ice off Rausu, the only place on the peninsula where drift-ice cruises depart. Rausu cruises run from late January to early March and are the group's best chance to see the eagles at close range.

photographer: No machine-readable author provided. ほくなん assumed (based on copyright claims).
attribution: No machine-readable author provided. ほくなん assumed (based on copyright claims). — Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Red-crowned cranes at the Tsurumidai feeding ground in Tsurui
caption: Red-crowned cranes (tancho) at the Tsurumidai feeding ground in Tsurui. Winter feeding runs from about mid-November to late March, so February and March both offer cranes standing on snow and displaying.

photographer: Alastair Rae from London, United Kingdom
attribution: Alastair Rae from London, United Kingdom — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Several red-crowned cranes standing in a snowy field
caption: A group of red-crowned cranes in the snow on the eastern Hokkaido plain. Feeding stations at Tsurui are public and the cranes are wild: keep to the marked viewing areas.

commonsFile: File:Lake Mashū Japan during wintertime in Akan National Park Hokkaidō.jpg
attribution: Kpravin2 — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Snow-covered Lake Mashū crater lake in winter
caption: Lake Mashū in winter. A caldera lake with no inlet or outlet, it is reached by short drives from Lake Kussharo and is a viewpoint stop on the day between Kawayu and Lake Akan.

attribution: Yuya Enjo — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
caption: Lake Kussharo in February, Japan's largest caldera lake. Whooper swans overwinter on its ice-free hot-spring patches, and the sand-bath shore at Sunayu is on the same lake.

commonsFile: File:Lake Akan shore in early winter.jpg
attribution: ブルーノ・プラス — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The shore of Lake Akan in early winter with snow and forest
caption: The shore of Lake Akan, where the group spends two nights. The lake freezes hard enough for guided walks and ice fishing, and Akanko Onsen and the Ainu Kotan village sit on its south shore.

commonsFile: File:コタン温泉（Kotan, outdoor bath） - panoramio.jpg
attribution: pakku — CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: An outdoor hot-spring bath at Kotan beside Lake Akan
caption: An outdoor onsen at the Kotan side of Lake Akan. Akan Ainu Kotan is a living village of craft shops and a theatre, one of the places in Hokkaido where Ainu people present their own culture.

alt: Upopoy National Ainu Museum and Park by Lake Poroto
caption: Upopoy, the national Ainu museum and park at Shiraoi, 10 minutes' walk from the station. It is the best single introduction to Ainu history and language before the group visits Akan, and it is closed on Mondays and from 27 February to 8 March.

attribution: MaedaAkihiko — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The Kushiro River winding through the Kushiro Marsh wetland
caption: The Kushiro Marsh, Japan's largest wetland, seen from above the Kushiro River. In winter its observation decks look over snow-covered reeds and are the last stop before the flight home from Kushiro.
